title: Beef Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
summary: Tender beef meatballs, kept moist with a soaked-bread panade, are browned in the oven then finished gently in a simple garlic and chilli tomato sauce.
equipment: rimmed baking tray lined with baking paper
large deep frying pan or sauté pan with a lid (28 cm)

ingredients.item: day-old white bread, crusts removed, torn into small pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: about 1 tsp; only if the tomatoes taste sharp

steps.title: Make the panade
steps.text: Soak the torn bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then mash it to a smooth paste with a fork. This soaked starch acts like a sponge inside the meatballs, holding onto moisture so they stay tender even once fully cooked through.

steps.title: Mix and shape
steps.text: Add the beef mince, egg, 30g of the parmesan, grated garlic, parsley, and the meatball salt and pepper to the bread paste. Mix with your hands for about 1 minute, just until evenly combined and slightly tacky — overworking it at this stage makes the meatballs dense rather than light. With wet hands, roll into 20 balls of about 50g each, set on the oiled, lined tray, and chill for 15 minutes while the oven heats to 220°C (200°C fan).

steps.title: Brown in the oven
steps.text: Roast the meatballs for 12-14 minutes, until browned on top. Baking them this way colours them evenly on all sides without turning or splashing hot fat, and they'll finish cooking through once they go into the sauce.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in the large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6-8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute, then stir in the passata, sauce salt and sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp, and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavours settle together.

steps.title: Simmer and serve
steps.text: Add the browned meatballs and any tray juices to the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until a probe thermometer in the centre of a large meatball reads 71°C. Tear over the basil leaves and serve with the extra parmesan.

tips: Mix the meat mixture with a light hand — a minute of mixing is enough, and squeezing or overworking it makes the meatballs tough rather than tender.
Browning the meatballs in the oven first means they hold their shape better in the sauce than if they went in raw.
If the passata tastes sharp, a small spoon of sugar rounds it out — taste before adding it, as not every tin needs it.
safety: Use a probe thermometer to check 71°C in the centre of the largest meatball, since mince needs to be cooked through fully rather than judged by colour.
storage: Keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat in a covered pan over low heat, or in the microwave, stirring occasionally, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
